gloss: to deduct; to subtract; to balance

definitions.explanation: To remove an amount from a total, typically in financial or mathematical contexts.
To consider both positive and negative factors and arrive at a net result.

examples.japanese: {税金|ぜいきん}を{差|さ}し{引|ひ}いた{手取|てど}りは{20万円|にじゅうまんえん}です。
examples.english: The take-home pay after deducting taxes is 200,000 yen.

examples.japanese: {経費|けいひ}を{差|さ}し{引|ひ}くと{利益|りえき}はほとんどない。
examples.english: After deducting expenses, there's almost no profit.

notes:
CONJUGATION:
・{差|さ}し{引|ひ}く → {差|さ}し{引|ひ}かない (negative)
・{差|さ}し{引|ひ}く → {差|さ}し{引|ひ}いて (te-form)
・{差|さ}し{引|ひ}く → {差|さ}し{引|ひ}いた (past)

FORMATION:
Compound verb: {差|さ}す (to insert) + {引|ひ}く (to pull/subtract)

RELATED EXPRESSIONS:
・{差|さ}し{引|ひ}き - noun form meaning "deduction" or "balance"
・{差|さ}し{引|ひ}き{勘定|かんじょう} - net calculation/balance
・{差|さ}し{引|ひ}きゼロ - balances out to zero

USAGE:
Commonly used in financial and business contexts:
・{源泉徴収|げんせんちょうしゅう}を{差|さ}し{引|ひ}く (to deduct withholding tax)
・{割引|わりびき}を{差|さ}し{引|ひ}く (to deduct a discount)
